# KS3 Curriculum Redesign

The department's rebuild of Years 7 to 9 history around enquiries: 15 units, five a year, each driven by an [[enquiry-question]] and taught from in-house booklets. Umbrella for the audit, the Year 7 units, the Year 9 local history enquiry and the assessment model. Led by [[priyanka-sethi]] as Key Stage 3 lead, with me writing most of the Year 7 and Year 9 material.

## Outcome

A Years 7 to 9 curriculum of 15 enquiries, each year opening with two timeline lessons, fully taught from September 2026 and reviewed in July 2027.

## Current State

- All three years are on the new curriculum from September 2026. Year 7 has had it since September 2025, so the current Year 8 is the first group to have done two years of it.
- Every year group started the year with two timeline lessons and keeps a cumulative timeline in the back of their books. This is the compromise from the [[ks3-curriculum-review-2025-06-25]]; [[desmond-hartigan]] still thinks it is not enough and says so.
- Year 9's ropeworks enquiry is the last unit not yet taught; first teaching is spring term 2027 ([[local-history-enquiry]]).
- The common assessment model is paused until the trust sets its data collection calendar ([[ks3-assessment-model]]).
- Booklets replaced a textbook purchase in June 2025 ([[textbook-procurement]]); printing runs at about 1,450 GBP a year from the department budget.

## Scope and Boundaries

Years 7 to 9 only. The Key Stage 4 option choice is in [[thematic-study-switch]]. The oral history recordings themselves belong to the society ([[ropeworks-voices]]); this Project only uses clips that the consent forms allow for education.

## Working Context

The old schemes (written in 2019, mostly a chronological march with a topic per half-term) gave pupils a lot of coverage and very little practice at arguing. [[ruth-calder]] wanted enquiries; Desmond wanted chronology kept. The [[diverse-curriculum-audit]] in spring 2025 added a third pressure: whose stories the units tell. The design that came out of it:

- Five enquiries a year. Each takes roughly six weeks, has one assessed piece, a booklet and fortnightly retrieval quizzes in [[quillyard]].
- Each enquiry targets one second-order concept ([[second-order-concepts]]) and carries a fixed body of substantive knowledge ([[substantive-and-disciplinary-knowledge]]).
- Two timeline lessons open each year, and pupils add every enquiry to a cumulative timeline ([[chronological-framework]]).
- The sequence is in [[ks3-curriculum-map-2026-27]]; the planning steps for a new unit in [[plan-an-enquiry-unit]].

Pupil voice from Year 7 in July 2026 was positive about the booklets and mixed about the timeline lessons ([[ks3-pupil-voice-survey-2026-07]]). The early evidence on retention is thin; see [[how-much-do-pupils-remember-of-enquiries-a-year-later]].

## Active Workflows

- Priyanka chairs a Key Stage 3 slot at each department meeting.
- Booklet drafts live on the shared drive ([[history-department-shared-drive]]); [[bethan-lloyd-hughes]] checks sources and reading levels before printing.
- Each new enquiry gets one cycle of teaching before we revise it, not mid-unit rewrites.

## Next Actions

- [ ] Finish the Year 9 ropeworks enquiry booklet and clip set by 2026-12-18 ([[local-history-enquiry]]).
- [ ] Run the one-year retention check on the current Year 8 in January 2027 ([[how-much-do-pupils-remember-of-enquiries-a-year-later]]).
- [ ] Draft the July 2027 review plan with Priyanka for the December department meeting.
- [ ] Revisit the assessment model when the trust calendar is published ([[ks3-assessment-model]]).
